comment: Numeric ratchet manifest (DR-27a). Two arrays, two directions, one mechanism — tests/guards/numeric-floor-manifest.test.ts enforces both. `floors` entries may RISE, never fall. `ceilings` entries may be LOWERED, never raised: a budget or a maximum that can be raised to fit whatever the artifact grew into is not a budget, it asserts that the current size is the current size. Each entry pins a value AND the number of sites spelling it: the guard requires at least `occurrences` matches of `pattern` in `sourceFile`, so moving one site out of several is caught. New entries are allowed in either array; move `floor`/`ceiling`, `pattern` and `occurrences` together, and only in the permitted direction. Equality baselines (the GIT_MD_* / SKILL_* / TOTAL_* constants in tests/goldens/github-status-lines.test.ts) ratchet in neither direction and are not registered here.

floors.description: Number of compiled MDS host commands in dist/commands/ (MDS_COMMAND_HOSTS). The discovery assertion is a set-equality against tests/fixtures/mds-manifest.ts and this floor is that manifest's length, asserted alongside the set: the set says WHICH hosts, the floor says the roster may not shrink behind it. The pattern names its RECEIVER because partial-count in the same file now pins the same number: two entries sharing one bare pattern have no per-entry accounting, and the decrement probe of each would keep finding the other's site.

Number of .mds partial files anywhere under src/ (ALL_MDS_PARTIALS = MDS_PARTIALS under src/assets/commands/_partials/, plus MDS_REFERENCE_PARTIALS elsewhere). The discovery assertion is a set-equality against tests/fixtures/mds-manifest.ts over a repo-wide walk that classifies by the build's own rule -- no output-dir: key -- so a partial parked outside _partials/ is named rather than merely counted; this floor is its length. Floors rise with the roster, never fall — a partial deleted rather than inlined takes its callers with it silently.

DIST_FILES count = COMMAND_HOSTS (13) + release.md (1); DIST_FILES vs COMMAND_HOSTS divergence is permanent (SG-13). Five sites spell it, including the `<!-- devflow:` marker negative guard, which asserts both the built file count and its own distFilesScanned counter — the value is one number and the occurrence count is what stops one site drifting out of the set.

Minimum timeout in ms for the slow shell-exec tests that spawn scripts/build-mds.ts. Three sites, all negative-path spawns in this file: two dest-safety refusals and the ignored-dir walk. Every other isolated MDS build routes through buildCommittedTree(), whose own timeout is pinned by the mds-build-spawn-timeout-ms entry below.

Minimum timeout in ms for runMdsBuild() — the one spawn site every isolated MDS build now routes through, including buildCommittedTree(). Same floor as slow-test-timeout-ms, in the file the sites moved to.
Minimum number of subagent_type literal sites across dist+scripts corpus (currently ~66+)
MAX_CHARTER_CHARS = 75% of the 4096-char shell injection cap; orchestrator charter must stay at or below this
Minimum number of DEVFLOW_PLUGINS registry entries
Minimum install-path references in dist/commands/ files

D11 forward guard: posting ops (--body-file / -F body=@) that must reference Comment-sink scrub (D11), counted over the sink corpus gitAgentSinkCorpus() returns -- the resolved Git agent UNIONED with dist/skills/git/references/*.md, sliced in extractOpSection mode 'union' [DR-18]. The union is load-bearing: posting mechanics live in the generated references, so a git.md-only count would drop below the floor for reasons that are not a regression. The plugin-count entry above pins a different >= 8 in a different file.

resolveAllAgents() size — every DEVFLOW_PLUGINS agent resolves through the shared resolver (AC-0.7, GAP-07). 17 includes the hook-spawned Tracker agent, which is declared in devflow-core-skills.agents and filtered at install time rather than held outside the roster. A floor may only rise.
Operations indexed from git.md by the seam test's op→section map [DR-24]
Operations with at least one live caller fence. Directions 1 and 2 iterate this map; if it empties, both pass vacuously (the defect this floor exists to make loud).

KEYS in issue_capture_contract() checked by the seam test's producer direction. Six: the three original keys plus ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_PR_LINK and ISSUE_BRANCH_TOKEN, whose producers are the `### Handoff Values` block setup-task and fetch-issue emit. ISSUE_URL has no producer in git.md and is deliberately out. The direction is checked PER PRODUCER OP rather than over a concatenation, so it ranges over more (key, op) pairs than there are keys; the key count is what this floor pins.
manage-debt archive character cap (60 000 chars) — 4 tests assert this value; lowering one test out of the set is caught
D10 dedup-marker guard: two >= 2 floors in git-agent.test.ts (post-review-summary and post-resolution-summary dedup markers); lowering either site is caught

AC-0.10 containment guard (issue-body): ops wrapping remote issue content in <untrusted-issue-body> — setup-task, fetch-issue, fetch-issues-batch. The pattern names this entry's id so it matches ONE site: the sibling containment-external-thread-floor pins the same value 3 in the same file, and a bare toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3) at occurrences 2 is satisfied by the pair jointly, each entry's count met by the OTHER entry's assertion with neither site individually accounted for (PF-018).

AC-0.10 containment guard (external-thread): ops carrying <external-thread> for review thread bodies — fetch-review-threads, post-resolution-summary, post-wave-report. Pattern narrowed to this entry's own site for the reason recorded on the sibling containment-issue-body-floor entry above: two entries sharing one pattern in one file have no per-entry accounting.

BUILD/TARBALL SCOPE: the manifest the build EMITS, which is every provider. Distinct from installed-reference-count-{github,provider}, which pin what ONE install carries; the build stays at 34 so the tarball can serve any selection without a rebuild, and narrowing the install never lowers this floor. 34 = 10 GitHub ops + 10 Jira ops + 10 Linear ops (the SAME TRACKER_OPS roster, which is what makes file-set parity structural) + 3 cross-cutting documents + the tool-call contract, whose generation gate the first tool-call provider opens. Two sites — the manifest shape assertion and the 0644 normalisation's installed-file count. A manifest short enough to enumerate by hand makes every convergence assertion vacuous (GAP-42/PF-018), which is the same reason MIN_VARIANT_PAIRS exists. A floor may only rise, and here it rises by a whole provider at a time.

GAP-15 forwarding seam: Code-agent spawn sites carrying an ISSUE_NUMBER key across implement.md (8) and dynamic-build.md (6). The relational assertion -- every ISSUE_NUMBER payload also carries ISSUE_PR_LINK -- is vacuous over an empty or truncated payload set, so the site count is the non-vacuity floor and may only rise as spawn sites are added.

BUILD/TARBALL SCOPE (unaffected by the selection-scoped install): prefix-shippability clause (i) — the tarball must carry every file the reference overlay converges to. The floor keeps the packed-set assertion non-vacuous if the manifest is ever narrowed. It pins the same manifest as generated-reference-manifest-size at the OTHER sink, and the two must move together, or a provider could ship un-packed.

Total `**Process:**` / `### Process` blocks in the tracker corpus (dist/agents/git.md + the generated reference tree). The corpus split is asserted by provenance as well as by count: git.md's own contribution is 18, so a bare 18 was met with the generated tree entirely absent while the guard claimed to scan both (PF-018). 49 = git.md plus ten per-op references for each of the three providers, each with its own process block. A provider adds its whole roster at once, so the floor moves by a provider rather than by a file.

Minimum characters a generated tracker reference must carry, owned by tests/tracker/reference-floor.ts and imported by the three suites that measure that shape one step apart: reference-reachability.test.ts (the GitHub tree), linear-module.test.ts (the Linear tree) and jira-module.test.ts (the Jira tree plus the `@define` body the generator reads). One owner because a number spelled at each site can drift at one of them while every other site and a presence-only guard stay green. Registered as a FLOOR, not a ceiling: every assertion reading it is `content.length < MIN_REFERENCE_CHARS` → problem, so raising it makes all three suites stricter, while LOWERING it is the weakening move — it re-admits the shape the constant exists to catch, a reference that kept its heading and lost its body. Its own JSDoc names it a floor.

Column-0 `## ` lines the live generated reference tree must carry INSIDE a code fence, so the PF-063 structure guard's absence assertion is exercised against real fenced headings rather than a corpus that has none. Today: manage-debt.md's `## Items` (1) plus ensure-traceable-issue.md's heredoc and D3-template headings (6). Lowering it re-admits a corpus in which fence-awareness is proven only by the synthetic probes in tests/guards/agent-source-resolver.test.ts.

Rows HOSTILE_PAYLOADS must carry — seven register payloads, each targeting a different sink (command substitution in two spellings, flag injection, line injection, size, credential-in-URL, query-operator escape), plus the two identity payloads that are the only rows exercising `## Assignee`'s second prohibition. Registered as a FLOOR because the payload grid grades every row against every schema cell: a row ADDED widens the evidence and must never cost a suite failure, while a row REMOVED narrows the sinks the grid covers with nothing else reporting it. Spelled as an exact count it was the ratchet inverted — adding a payload, the thing a reviewer most wants a contributor to do, failed the suite.

Rows HOSTILE_REFS must carry — shell separator, command substitution, both flag-injection spellings, path traversal, size, the zero-numbered key an unanchored digit class admits, and whitespace. Every pinned grammar in PROVIDER_REF_GRAMMARS is driven over the whole table, so one row added widens the corpus for every provider at once and one removed silently narrows it for all of them. A FLOOR for the same reason as min-hostile-payloads.

Distinct devflow: skill references across the widened closure corpus (dist/commands + agent sources + skill bodies incl. references/). Non-vacuity floor for the bidirectional requires: guard — a scanner that stopped matching would make both arms pass over an empty corpus. Measured 2026-09-19: 200 files, 297 sites, 44 distinct.

Reference files ONE github install carries: the tracker/github tree plus the provider-independent cross-cutting documents. Install-time scope, distinct from the build-time 34 below, which is unchanged — the build still emits every provider so the tarball can serve any selection without a rebuild. Measured 2026-09-19: 13 files / 31,399 B.

Reference files ONE jira or linear install carries: github (13, the PR-host floor) + the selected provider (11). Excludes tracker/_mcp.md from the count assertion path, which is asserted biconditionally instead. Install-time scope, distinct from the build-time 34 below. Measured 2026-09-19: jira 24 files / 69,252 B, linear 24 / 73,501 B.

ceilings.description: THE PHASE-2 BASE the live git.md gate is derived from; budget-git-md-p3 below is that gate. Max characters of dist/agents/git.md at the Phase-2 boundary: derived from the post-Phase-0 baseline capture less the cut Phase 2 projected for it (no per-component decomposition is recorded — three successive re-derivations of those components disagreed, PF-057), pinned at 55_900, then LOWERED to 55_750 after the Mechanics-pointer condensing pass (measured 55_664, headroom 86). Kept registered because the live git.md gate budget-git-md-p3 is COMPUTED from it, and because a companion arm holds the portion of git.md outside the preamble to this value less PREAMBLE_CHARS_P2. Still may never be raised. No threshold is lowered, and a budget raised to fit the artifact is not a budget.

Max characters of dist/agents/git.md for PHASE 3 [DR-13(b)] — the live git.md gate. A NEW entry, not a raise of budget-git-md: a ceiling may only be re-derived downward, so the Phase-2 value stays pinned and this one is re-derived from it by the MEASURED growth of the preamble block (measured 58_818, headroom 52 — the same deliberate thinness). The revision is itemised clause by clause in the constant's own JSDoc: the four-step provider resolution order, ref-grammar corroboration with its prohibition on reading the remote, the project-key chain, the provider-mismatch guard, four DEGRADED arms and the input-contract section list, less the retired Phase-2 scope sentence and two de-duplicated rules. [DR-13(c)]'s _resolution.md escape was measured and rejected: moving text into a per-op-summed reference is NET ZERO on the loaded-set gate, and the only classification that would reduce it treats a containment control as an optional load (PF-058). The revision is spendable on the preamble ONLY, and mechanically so: a companion gate holds the portion of git.md outside the preamble to the UNRAISED BUDGET_GIT_MD minus PREAMBLE_CHARS_P2, so growth in an operation section still goes red against Phase 2's number, and a cut there widens that margin instead of consuming this ceiling. No per-pass decomposition of that portion is recorded — three successive re-derivations of those components disagreed (PF-057), so re-run tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts for the current figures: the ceilings are the assertion, the printed table is the record. May be LOWERED, never raised.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn under the JIRA provider — its own row, never folded into budget-loaded-set. The GitHub row keeps bytes(tracker/_mcp.md) = 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, so pricing a provider that DOES load the contract on that row would bill every GitHub user for bytes they never receive (GAP-02). ONE-TIME RE-BASELINE 2026-09-20 under an explicit authorisation, recorded as such because a ceiling is otherwise lowered and never raised (PF-071): the previous 88_660 was set before the tool-call contract grew, and that growth was never priced. What the raise bought lands entirely in references/tracker/_mcp.md, which went 6_907 -> 7_963 ch: the two-server per-capability scoping rule (partition by the tool name's leading namespace segment, per-capability qualification, unique-winner-else-DEGRADED, spawn-pinned affinity, and the corroborating read a write requires), the rate-limit signals section, the Reference Rendering rule, and the plan artifact posted as content with an over-cap DEGRADED path. Measured from the shape table tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints, shape '2-jira. per-op split, jira path': measured 89_459, pinned at 89_500, headroom 41 as of this measurement — re-run the test for the current figure, since it narrows every time git.md, the contract, or a jira op reference grows. The companion 'not a free number' arm is retired with the re-baseline: it held the delta over a GitHub ceiling that was itself derived, and neither row is derived any more. LOWERED THEREAFTER, NEVER RAISED AGAIN — trimming references/tracker/_mcp.md is the sanctioned first response, condensing the jira mechanics the second. budget-loaded-set-linear is the sibling row; a registered MCP-backed provider with no such entry fails a named arm in the same file.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn under the LINEAR provider — its own row, for the reason the jira row is one (D-LOADED-SET-PER-PROVIDER). ONE-TIME RE-BASELINE 2026-09-20 on the same explicit authorisation and for the same unpriced growth of references/tracker/_mcp.md as budget-loaded-set-jira, whose description records what the raise bought term by term; recorded as a re-baseline because a ceiling is otherwise lowered and never raised (PF-071). Measured from the shape table tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints, shape '2-linear. per-op split, linear path': measured 91_642, pinned at 91_700, headroom 58 as of this measurement — re-run the test for the current figure. This is still the binding constraint on any addition to the always-loaded agent, since a character added to git.md is a character added to every row. This provider's max_op is the largest of the three for a recorded reason rather than by accident: backlink-shipped-issues is where the dedup ladder is stated, and on a stock official server three of its four rungs are unreachable (OD-12), so each rung's unavailability plus both halves of the rank-4 marker predicate have to be written down. The companion 'not a free number' arm is retired with the re-baseline. LOWERED THEREAFTER, NEVER RAISED AGAIN.

Max characters of src/assets/skills/git/SKILL.md, derived at design time from the pre-split capture of that file less the projected cut, and pinned to that derivation rather than re-derived from whatever the file measures today. The skill carries doctrine, not mechanics: anything that grows it back past this is mechanics that belong in a generated reference. May be LOWERED, never raised.

Max characters of the worst-case tracker spawn on the GITHUB path, where bytes(tracker/_mcp.md) is 0 by construction (no github op file names the contract; the re-scoped AC-2.7 arm in tests/guards/provider-scope.test.ts proves it). ONE-TIME RE-BASELINE 2026-09-20 under an explicit authorisation, recorded as such because a ceiling is otherwise lowered and never raised (PF-071): it was the frozen PRE-SPLIT preloaded set of 77_824 with a computed phase-paired companion layered on top, and both are retired in favour of one number gating the shipped shape. What the raise bought is the per-op split itself — the monolith loaded one document, the split loads the agent plus the operation's own mechanics plus whatever cross-cutting references that operation can name in one spawn, and that sum is larger than the monolith was. Measured from the shape table tests/tracker/byte-budget.test.ts prints, shape '2. per-op split, GitHub path': measured 80_155, pinned at 80_200, headroom 45 as of this measurement — re-run the test for the current figure rather than trusting a number restated here. LOWERED THEREAFTER, NEVER RAISED AGAIN: the sanctioned response to it going red is moving text out of the agent or condensing the github mechanics.

AC-2.5 [DR-13(a)] — max lines of the provider-resolution preamble, which is preloaded on every Git spawn. LOWERED 40 -> 36 on 2026-09-20 against a measured 35: the permitted direction, and the only direction this ceiling has ever moved in (a proposal to raise it to 70 was refused as strictly weaker than the assertion already in place). One line of headroom is deliberate — the next rule added to the preamble must retire one. May be LOWERED, never raised.

EC-17 — max characters of the Section-3 tracker directive TEMPLATE as spelled in src/assets/scripts/hooks/session-start-context. additionalContext is re-sent on every qualifying session start, so the directive length is a per-session cost. Measured 722 at the pin, headroom 78. Pinned against the hook SOURCE rather than the emitted text because the emitted text carries two absolute paths whose length is a property of the caller tmpdir, not of the directive. May be LOWERED after a pass that actually cuts the text, never raised: a cap raised to fit whatever the directive grew into is not a cap.
